title: Cast iron and stone
blurb: A cast-iron spiral stair and a Gothic arcade, built live by JSON commands, then a realism pass.
intro: Two pieces built live through the modelling command API. A cast-iron spiral stair to a dealer's catalogue numbers (53" diameter, 8" rise, 12 treads a turn): one lathed column, one hand-made tread repeated by a live radial array, balusters on the same array, a handrail swept along the computed helix. A Gothic arcade from HABS drawings of the Church of the Ascension, New York: a pointed arch from two arcs, a clustered pier, a rib vault, bays on live linear arrays and a live mirror for the far side. Then a realism pass with the realism kit.
compareIntro: No geometry rebuilt (30-minute budget). Cast iron: the metal-dark preset (roughness 0.55) with a cast-surface relief at a 3 cm tile; the stair was painted off-white before. Arcade: limestone with a tooled relief at a 0.5 m tile (the kit has no stone pattern yet: grain stands in), the darker stone on bases, abaci, string course and ribs. Aisle floor: 0.9 m flagstone joints as groove strips - the floor is a plane, so cut: false lays the strips without the boolean.

metricsFirst: 297 commands headless in Node (no film), 0 failed, 15/15 checks. The film's 222 differ: its camera moves are eased by the film and not counted, and the recording branch grows the arrays one step at a time
metrics: claude-opus-5-5 · 315 tool calls · 179k output / 104M input tokens
how:
build.mjs is the demo's session build script (catalogue and HABS readings, then the build, then measured checks). The realism pass is a block in its finale (session.realism, on by default). record.mjs runs it unchanged in examples/modelling-api on the GPU VM through demos/shared/session.mjs and demos/shared/film.mjs (every frame rendered and captured; camera jumps eased; captures held with their captions). The sun's shadow camera is sized by the film.

Re-run: node demos/stair/record.mjs then node demos/shared/report.mjs demos/stair. Only the public-domain HABS drawings appear on screen; the dealer's photographs of the stair (all rights reserved) were local modelling references and are not shown.
weak: The stair's tread casting is a pierced grid, not the catalogue's ornamental pattern; balusters are plain lathes.
The arcade has no wall behind it, no clerestory, no capitals' foliage: the mouldings are bevels, not profiles from a moulding library (R3 is not built yet).
Stone relief is the plastic-grain pattern at a large tile; no ashlar coursing on the piers or spandrels.
Cast iron reads as dark metal; a painted cast-iron preset (low metalness, semi-gloss) would be closer.
